templates.name: backrest
templates.title: Backrest (restic)
templates.description: Deduplicated, encrypted restic backups with a web UI and schedules, e.g. offsite to a Storage Box over SFTP or any rclone remote. Docker volumes are mounted read-only under /userdata/volumes. Create the admin account on first start.

inputs.name: EXTRA_PATH
inputs.title: Additional host folder to back up (read-only)

templates.name: binfmt
templates.title: Foreign-architecture emulation
templates.description: Registers QEMU user-mode emulators, so images built for another CPU (e.g. amd64 on an arm64 host) can run, slower. The NepFleet agent re-runs it after each boot (registrations do not survive a reboot). Privileged.

templates.name: caddy
templates.title: Caddy ingress
templates.description: Reverse proxy with automatic TLS. Routes are read from caddy.* labels, and DNS-01 gives trusted certificates on home networks too.

inputs.name: CADDY_DNS_PROVIDER
inputs.title: DNS provider for DNS-01
inputs.description: Needed for trusted certificates on names that are not reachable from the internet (home network) and for wildcards.

inputs.name: DNS_API_TOKEN
inputs.title: DNS provider API token
inputs.description: Leave empty when the provider is none.

templates.name: dozzle
templates.title: Dozzle
templates.description: Live container logs in the browser. Deploy on swarm for a fleet-wide view.

templates.name: frpc
templates.title: frp client (home side)
templates.description: Publishes a local service through an frps on a public host. Add more [[proxies]] to frpc.toml in the fleet repository.

inputs.name: SERVER_ADDR
inputs.title: frps address
inputs.description: The public host's WireGuard IP.

inputs.name: FRP_TOKEN
inputs.title: frps token
inputs.description: The FRP_TOKEN generated for the frps stack.

inputs.name: LOCAL_HOST
inputs.title: Local service host
inputs.description: Container name on the ingress network (e.g. jellyfin) or an IP.

templates.name: frps
templates.title: frp server (public side)
templates.description: Receives tunnels from frpc at home and publishes them through Caddy. Bind it to the WireGuard address, so the control port is never on the internet.

inputs.name: BIND_ADDR
inputs.title: Address for the frp control port
inputs.description: This host's WireGuard IP (recommended) or 0.0.0.0.

inputs.name: EXPOSED_HOSTS
inputs.title: Public host names served through tunnels
inputs.description: Comma separated, e.g. "jellyfin.example.org, photos.example.org"

templates.name: homepage
templates.title: Homepage
templates.description: A dashboard for your services. Entries come from homepage.* labels; title, theme, language, search and the resource widgets are set as values (NepFleet owns settings.yaml and widgets.yaml; bookmarks.yaml and the rest stay yours).

templates.name: neptide
templates.title: neptide image updates
templates.description: Health-gated image updates with automatic rollback, for containers and swarm services labelled neptide.enable=true.

inputs.name: DOCKER_GID
inputs.title: Group id of the docker group on the host
inputs.description: getent group docker | cut -d: -f3

inputs.name: NOTIFY
inputs.title: Notification URLs
inputs.description: Comma separated shoutrrr URLs, e.g. discord://token@webhookid

templates.name: uptime-kuma
templates.title: Uptime Kuma + AutoKuma
templates.description: Uptime monitoring and status pages. AutoKuma creates monitors from kuma.* labels. Install it once for the whole fleet, or once per stack for a stack-local status page.

inputs.name: KUMA_USERNAME
inputs.title: Admin user
inputs.description: Create this user in Uptime Kuma's first-run screen. AutoKuma logs in with it.

templates.name: volume-backup
templates.title: Volume backups (docker-volume-backup)
templates.description: Scheduled, age-encrypted backups of the Docker volumes on this host, to a local folder and optionally over SSH/SFTP (e.g. a Storage Box). Containers labelled docker-volume-backup.stop-during-backup=true are stopped during the backup for consistency. Host folders (media, photos) are not included; back them up with backrest.

inputs.name: AGE_RECIPIENTS
inputs.title: age public keys (comma separated)
inputs.description: Use the recipients from fleet.yaml spec.secrets.age, so the fleet's key can decrypt every backup.

inputs.name: SSH_HOST_NAME
inputs.title: SSH/SFTP host for off-host copies (empty = local only)

inputs.name: SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY
inputs.title: SSH host public key
inputs.description: Required with SSH. One line from `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 -p <port> <host>`, without the host name, e.g. "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…".

inputs.name: EXCLUDE_REGEXP
inputs.title: Paths to skip (regular expression)
inputs.description: Volumes that hold only caches or downloadable data, matched against /backup/volumes/<name>/...

inputs.name: NOTIFICATION_URLS
inputs.title: Notification URLs (shoutrrr, comma separated)
inputs.description: Failed backups are always reported here, e.g. discord://token@webhookid

templates.name: watchtower
templates.title: Watchtower (maintained fork)
templates.description: Image update notifications for containers NepFleet does not manage. Monitor-only by default, because in-place updates bypass the fleet repository and cannot be rolled back.

inputs.name: WATCHTOWER_MODE
inputs.title: Mode
inputs.description: "true" = monitor only (notify). "false" = update labelled containers in place.

inputs.name: NOTIFICATION_URL
inputs.title: Notification URL
inputs.description: A shoutrrr URL, e.g. ntfy://ntfy.sh/my-topic

templates.name: actual
templates.title: Actual Budget
templates.description: Local-first personal finance and envelope budgeting. Set the server password on the first visit.

templates.name: audiobookshelf
templates.title: Audiobookshelf
templates.description: Audiobook and podcast server with apps for phones, progress sync and podcast downloads. Create the root user on the first visit.

inputs.name: AUDIOBOOKS_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder with your audiobooks
inputs.description: Mounted writable, so uploads, metadata embedding and deleting files from the app work.

inputs.name: PODCASTS_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder for podcasts (downloads go here)

templates.name: bookstack
templates.title: BookStack
templates.description: Wiki and documentation, organised in shelves, books and pages. Sign in with admin@admin.com / password on the first visit and change both right away.

templates.name: forgejo
templates.title: Forgejo + Actions runner
templates.description: Self-hosted git forge with a registered Forgejo Actions runner. Jobs run in an isolated Docker-in-Docker daemon, never on the host's Docker.

inputs.name: SSH_PORT
inputs.title: Host port for git over SSH

templates.name: homeassistant
templates.title: Home Assistant
templates.description: Home automation. Runs on host networking for device discovery (mDNS, SSDP), and Caddy reaches it through host.docker.internal. Not for swarm.

inputs.name: ZIGBEE_DEVICE
inputs.title: Zigbee USB stick for ZHA (e.g. SkyConnect, Sonoff)
inputs.description: Pick its /dev/serial/by-id path; Home Assistant sees the same path, so ZHA keeps working across reboots. After replugging the stick, restart the stack.

templates.name: homebox
templates.title: Homebox
templates.description: Home inventory and organisation.

inputs.name: ALLOW_REGISTRATION
inputs.title: Allow registration
inputs.description: Needed to create the first account; turn off afterwards.

templates.name: immich
templates.title: Immich (+ Power Tools)
templates.description: Photo and video backup with machine learning. Immich Power Tools (bulk management, login with your Immich account) is an optional profile. Photos live in UPLOAD_PATH on the host; back that folder up with backrest (volume-backup covers the database).

inputs.name: UPLOAD_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder for photos and videos

templates.name: jellyfin
templates.title: Jellyfin
templates.description: Media server. Mount your media read-only. Pick a GPU for hardware transcoding.

inputs.name: GPU
inputs.title: Hardware transcoding (VAAPI/QSV on Intel or AMD, NVENC on NVIDIA)

templates.name: kutt
templates.title: Kutt
templates.description: URL shortener (SQLite).

templates.name: mealie
templates.title: Mealie
templates.description: Recipe manager and meal planner that imports recipes from any URL. Sign in with changeme@example.com / MyPassword on the first visit and change the email and password right away: until then anyone can log in as admin.

templates.name: metube
templates.title: MeTube (yt-dlp web UI)
templates.description: Download videos and audio with yt-dlp from the browser. No built-in login, so keep it on the home network or behind forward auth.

templates.name: n8n
templates.title: n8n
templates.description: Workflow automation with a visual editor, webhooks and hundreds of integrations.

inputs.name: DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain (also the base URL of webhooks)

templates.name: navidrome
templates.title: Navidrome
templates.description: Music streaming server with a Subsonic-compatible API. Music is mounted read-only.

templates.name: open-webui
templates.title: Open WebUI (+ Ollama, LiteLLM)
templates.description: Chat UI for language models. Profiles add Ollama (local models) and/or LiteLLM, an OpenAI-compatible gateway to cloud providers and other runtimes (vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI); models are configured in litellm.yaml. The first account becomes admin.

inputs.name: ENABLE_SIGNUP
inputs.title: Allow sign-ups
inputs.description: Applies on first start only; Open WebUI stores it, so later changes go through its Admin settings.

templates.name: opencloud
templates.title: OpenCloud
templates.description: File sync and share (stable channel).

templates.name: owncast
templates.title: Owncast
templates.description: Live streaming and chat. RTMP ingest is published directly on the host.

templates.name: paperless
templates.title: Paperless-ngx
templates.description: Document management with OCR.

inputs.name: CONSUME_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder watched for new documents

templates.name: rclone
templates.title: rclone
templates.description: Remote-control daemon with the web GUI for syncing to cloud storage (e.g. a Hetzner Storage Box). Remotes live in rclone.conf, which is stored encrypted in the fleet repository.

inputs.name: DATA_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder rclone may read and write

templates.name: registry
templates.title: Container registry
templates.description: Private OCI registry (CNCF Distribution) with htpasswd authentication.

inputs.name: HTPASSWD
inputs.title: htpasswd line(s)
inputs.description: bcrypt only, e.g. the output of `htpasswd -nB alice`.

templates.name: sendan
templates.title: Sendan
templates.description: Self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted file sharing.

inputs.name: DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain
inputs.description: Used in every share link. Must be the public address.

templates.name: stirling-pdf
templates.title: Stirling-PDF
templates.description: PDF toolbox in the browser (merge, split, convert, OCR, sign); files are processed on your server. With login on, sign in as admin with the generated ADMIN_PASSWORD (read it with: sops decrypt stacks/stirling-pdf/values.secret.yaml); you are asked to change it. Plan about 4 GB of memory.

inputs.name: ENABLE_LOGIN
inputs.title: Require a login (recommended when the domain is public)

templates.name: sweetfolio
templates.title: Sweetfolio
templates.description: Portfolio planning and evaluation. Static app; data stays in the browser.

templates.name: syncthing
templates.title: Syncthing
templates.description: Continuous file synchronisation between your devices, without a cloud. Sign in as admin with the generated GUI_PASSWORD (read it with: sops decrypt stacks/syncthing/values.secret.yaml). Add folders under /data, which is your host folder: it must exist and belong to PUID:PGID. Devices find each other through global discovery and relays (LAN broadcast does not cross Docker networks). With a SYNC_PORT other than 22000, set Listen Addresses to: default, tcp://<host>:SYNC_PORT, quic://<host>:SYNC_PORT.

inputs.name: DATA_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder that synced folders live in (/data in Syncthing)
inputs.description: Create it first and give it to PUID:PGID; a folder Docker creates belongs to root, and Syncthing cannot write there.

inputs.name: SYNC_PORT
inputs.title: Host port for device connections (TCP and UDP)

inputs.name: PUID
inputs.title: User id owning the synced files

inputs.name: PGID
inputs.title: Group id owning the synced files

templates.name: tdarr
templates.title: Tdarr
templates.description: Distributed media transcoding. Runs the server with an internal node; nodes on other hosts connect to the server port. Authentication stays on. Log in as admin with tapi_ followed by the generated API_KEY (read it with: sops decrypt stacks/tdarr/values.secret.yaml) and give remote nodes the same key. Pick a GPU for hardware transcoding.

inputs.name: MEDIA_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder with media to transcode

inputs.name: CACHE_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder for transcode cache (fast disk)

inputs.name: SERVER_PORT
inputs.title: Host port for remote Tdarr nodes

inputs.name: GPU
inputs.title: Hardware transcoding (VAAPI/QSV on Intel or AMD, NVENC on NVIDIA)

templates.name: vaultwarden
templates.title: Vaultwarden
templates.description: Bitwarden-compatible password manager.

inputs.name: ADMIN_TOKEN
inputs.title: Admin token (Argon2 PHC string)
inputs.description: Leave empty to disable /admin. Generate with `docker run --rm -it vaultwarden/server /vaultwarden hash`.
